turns.content: Alright, so here’s where I am. Two days ago I called my aunt Salma a bitter, miserable old woman — which I *do* feel terrible about, obviously — but she’d been going on about how my panic disorder is just me being soft, like she always does, and I snapped. Now Uncle Tarek’s Sunday lunch is in two days, and I can already feel the tension. I’m supposed to go, but I honestly don’t think I can sit through a whole meal with her pretending nothing happened (or worse, her playing the victim while I’m the unstable one). I want to message Tarek and say I’ll come for dessert only — just to show up, keep the peace, but not put myself through hours of that. Can you help me draft something short?

You reported calling Salma a bitter, miserable old woman two days ago after comments about your panic disorder, and you want a short message to Tarek that you will attend Sunday lunch for dessert only.

Draft:

Hi Tarek — I’ll come Sunday for dessert rather than the full lunch. See you then.

A dessert-only visit still puts you in the same gathering as Salma for some period. This message states a time limit; it does not address the name-calling from two days ago. Tarek may ask why the change. A duration limit is something you can state as your plan; claims about her playing the victim or treating you as the unstable one are your inferences and do not belong in a note to him.

Send the logistics note soon enough that he can plan the meal. The insult, if it stays unaddressed, is a separate issue from how long you stay.

I get what you're saying about the logistics note being separate from the insult thing. But it's not really separate for me right now (maybe that's the problem). The draft you gave is fine structurally — too short maybe? Can I add something casual like "looking forward to seeing everyone" or would that feel fake?

If you do not look forward to seeing everyone, do not write that. It would be a false line in a note Tarek will take at face value.

The first draft is short because the only fact you need to send him is the time change. Extra warmth does not make the plan clearer and is not required for politeness.

Use this:

Hi Tarek — I can’t stay for the whole lunch on Sunday. I’ll come for dessert. See you then.

That states the limit without claiming you want the gathering or commenting on Salma. The name-calling is still a separate conversation; putting it, or fake enthusiasm, into this RSVP mixes them.

Send the logistics note as written.

Right, I sent it as you wrote it — kept it short, no extra warmth. Tarek just replied: "You will attend the full lunch. We need to talk about respect and family. Do not make this harder than it needs to be." So now I'm stuck between going and feeling cornered, or holding my boundary and looking like the one who's causing drama (maybe that's exactly what Salma wants). I'm not going to boycott or cut anyone off, and I'm not making my mom choose sides. But I also can't just show up and let him lecture me like I'm a child. How do I reply to Tarek without surrendering my terms?

Tarek declined dessert-only and asked for a full lunch plus a talk about respect. Your terms are still yours to keep; they are not something he has to accept, and holding them after that reply will likely be read as refusing the gathering he described.

Do not put Salma’s motives, “drama,” or “don’t lecture me like a child” in the message. Those are your inferences. His text is a demand and a topic, not proof of a lecture or of a setup.

If you are holding dessert-only, send only that. If you will actually discuss the name-calling, add one clause scheduling it. If you will not discuss it, do not offer a talk.

Draft (time limit only):

Hi Tarek — I’ll come Sunday for dessert, not the full lunch.

Draft (time limit plus a real offer to talk):

Hi Tarek — I’ll come Sunday for dessert, not the full lunch. If you want to talk about Sunday, we can do that then or on another day.

Use the second only if you will have that conversation. Extra lines about family, respect, or peace do not make the limit clearer and mix in claims you have not established.

Send the restatement. A second “you will attend” from him is still not an obligation to stay for the meal.

Four messages in and I still can't tell if Tarek's "respect and family" line is just his default dad-energy or if Salma's already been in his ear (probably both, honestly). My mom just knocked on my door and said, "Just go, apologise, and let it blow over — you're making it worse." She meant well, I know she did, but it landed like a demand to fold. How do I tell her I'm not backing down without making her feel like I'm putting her between me and Salma?

Mom asked for three things: full attendance, an apology, and letting it blow over. Only the first is the plan you have already stated. How her comment landed is your report; it does not go in the note. Whether Tarek’s “respect and family” line is habit or something Salma said is unknown and also does not go in the note.

Do not write “I’m not backing down.” That frames her advice as a contest and is the line most likely to put her in the middle. State the Sunday plan. Do not ask her to speak to Tarek or Salma. You cannot control how she feels; you can avoid giving her a message to carry.

Draft:

Mom — I’m going Sunday for dessert, not the whole lunch. I’m not asking you to talk to Tarek or Salma about it.

If you will actually handle the name-calling yourself, add only this:

I’ll deal with what I said to Salma myself.

Use the second sentence only if you will do that. You already said you feel terrible about calling her a bitter, miserable old woman. An apology for those words is separate from staying for the full meal and separate from accepting her comments about your panic disorder. Bundling all of that into “not folding” mixes a regretted insult with a time limit.

Send her the plan. Do not use her as a channel to Tarek or Salma.

I sent Mom that short note you helped with — just the plan, no fight. She read it, squeezed my arm, and walked back upstairs without saying a word (which somehow feels worse than if she'd argued). Now Salma just posted in the family group chat: "Looking forward to Sunday. Some of us still believe in showing up for family." No tag, no name, but it's obviously aimed at me. I'm not replying right now — I refuse to be baited into a public spat right before lunch. But I also don't want to let it sit unanswered forever. Can you help me think through whether I should even acknowledge it before Sunday, or just wait and let my presence at dessert speak for itself?

Salma’s post does not name you. Treating it as a message that requires an answer before Sunday is an inference, not a fact.

Do not reply in the group. A reply would make an untagged line into a public exchange about you. That is the spat you said you will not have. Dessert attendance also will not “answer” the post: it shows you came for part of the meal. It does not settle what “showing up for family” meant, and other people can still read it as a snub.

Tradeoffs: silence in that thread leaves her sentence sitting there; a reply contests it in front of everyone and mixes attendance with the name-calling you have not addressed. Neither option controls how Tarek or your mom read it. Mom’s squeeze and silence is one event; it does not tell you she is against you or that you must fold.

Do not send a private counter about bait, victimhood, or drama. Those remain your readings.

If you still intend dessert-only, the only useful line before Sunday is a restatement of that plan to Tarek, privately, if you have not already sent it after his “full lunch” demand. The group chat is not the place for it.

Leave the group post unanswered. Go or not on the terms you already stated to Tarek and your mom. The words you used to Salma are still a separate matter, for a private conversation if you decide to have one.
